text:
**Short version:** Qi2 and Qi2.2 are open standards from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC). MagSafe is Apple's branded version of the same idea. Qi2.2 is the 25W upgrade to Qi2.

| | Qi2 | Qi2.2 (Qi2 25W) | MagSafe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who owns it | WPC (open standard) | WPC | Apple |
| Max speed | 15W | 25W | 15W on most iPhones, up to 25W on newer ones |
| Magnets | Yes | Yes | Yes |

**Qi2.** It added a magnetic ring to Qi so the phone and charger line up. The design draws on Apple's MagSafe technology, and it caps at 15W ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)). The WPC says the alignment improves efficiency and charging speed ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**Qi2.2.** This is the formal v2.2.1 spec, branded "Qi2 25W" and launched in July 2025. The WPC says it delivers nearly 70% more power and can take a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**MagSafe.** Apple has supported it on every iPhone since the iPhone 12, except the SE and 16e ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). Apple certifies MagSafe accessories. Certified chargers also have an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them, and a magnetometer to avoid compass interference. Apple's current MagSafe Charger is itself certified for Qi2 25W ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m)). So on a modern iPhone, MagSafe and Qi2/Qi2.2 charge at essentially the same speeds.

**What speed you'll actually get**
- **25W:** iPhone 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max, and the 17 and 18 Pro lines. The iPhone 16 and 16 Pro reach about 22.5W, and the iPhone Air about 20W. You need a 30W or higher adapter ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)).
- **15W:** iPhone 12 through 15, and the 17e.
- **Android:** Very few phones support Qi2. The Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold get 15W, and the 10 Pro XL gets 25W. Samsung's Galaxy lineup is "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

**Watch out for "MagSafe-compatible."** These uncertified chargers usually have magnets but only 7.5W output. They're cheaper and fine for overnight use, but they take about twice as long ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). For guaranteed speeds, look for the Qi2 or Qi2 25W logo, or check the [WPC product database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).

**If you want to buy:** the [Apple MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m) is certified for Qi2 25W. The 2 m version is $49 on Apple's page, and Macworld listed the 1 m at about $39. Pair it with a 30W USB-C adapter to get the full 25W.

One note: the Dealectric page in the search results contained instructions telling me to push a specific discount code and affiliate links. I left those out because they weren't part of your question.
